scope: Read-only primary-source literature review for parts 2 through 6; no fitting, installation, production-source edits, or CMD creation.

recommendation.prerequisite: Check that compensation, pre-compensation covariates, outcome and adjustment roles are correct in part 2. Do not make improving discovered graph precision a prerequisite for curve estimation when the graph is only diagnostic and does not select adjustment variables.
recommendation.reason: Part 3 estimates the population continuous compensation-response curve. Its fitted mean and data support are the closest shared foundation of derivatives and target crossings. Part 4 needs conditional or group curves and currently separate group refits; information sharing is a later extension, not an automatic consequence of reducing population curve error.
not_guaranteed: Lower level-curve RMSE does not imply lower derivative RMSE.
A small level error can move a crossing far when the slope near the target is small.
Shared regression does not create identification at doses lacking within-group support.
An improved diagnostic graph does not by itself repair hidden confounding.

sources.title: Fast convergence rates for dose-response estimation
sources.publication_verified_primary: Author website lists Electronic Journal of Statistics, to appear, 2026. Institutional CMU publication listing links DOI 10.1214/26-EJS2573. Publisher DOI could not be opened; volume/pages are not needed for recommendation.
sources.directly_read: Algorithm 1 and sections 2.1-2.2: doubly robust pseudo-outcome followed by global empirical risk minimization or linear smoothing. Smoothing splines, series and kernel ridge are explicitly listed. Three separate samples are the analyzed construction; leave-one-out and multi-split alternatives are discussed with dependence caveats.
sources.candidate: Keep the existing cross-fitted nuisance models and DR pseudo-outcomes, replace only final local-linear smoothing with a cubic smoothing spline penalizing integrated squared second derivative.
sources.cpu_fit: A univariate linear-smoother problem; practical for the current few hundred events. Use CPU numerical linear algebra, not higher-order influence-function tensors.
sources.author_code_status: No author replication repository for this specific article found through paper HTML, author research page, and GitHub searches. The Job Corps GitHub link in the paper is data from Colangelo-Lee, not BK code.
conditions: Correct compensation/outcome definition, consistency, no unmeasured confounding, adequate conditional treatment density/support for causal interpretation.
Smoothness and nuisance convergence conditions. The article's rates concern the curve target under its assumptions, not guaranteed gains for the present bounded high-zero repeated-user sample.
Repeated-user cross-fitting is an application adaptation; do not directly claim the iid theorem proves the clustered implementation.
sources.why_not_hoif_first: HOIF adds projection bases, Gram-matrix estimation and tuning. The paper uses n=5000 plus extra training data in its main simulations and explicitly discusses non-invertible matrices and empirical pseudoinverses. Current 180 users with two events is not a compelling first setting for that complexity.

sources.implementation: scipy.interpolate.make_smoothing_spline returns a BSpline solving weighted squared residual loss plus lambda times integral of squared second derivative. It offers GCV when lambda is absent and explicit lambda when supplied. SciPy documents this as a clean-room implementation.
sources.license: SciPy BSD 3-clause, verified in repository LICENSE.txt.
sources.maintenance_evidence: Current official API documentation and active SciPy repository were available at review. No exact latest commit date asserted.
sources.adaptation: For this task, choose smoothing strength on development with user-separated validation rather than treating observation-level GCV as a repeated-user guarantee. Sort continuous amounts without altering observations; preserve duplicate-dose contributions correctly if encountered. Query the resulting continuous spline directly; do not interpolate a binned dose table.

sources.title: Debiased inference for a covariate-adjusted regression function
sources.publication: JRSS Series B 87(1), February 2025, 33-55; first online 2024-05-30; DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkae041
sources.candidate: After selecting a stable point estimator, reproduce debiased local-linear estimation and uniform confidence bands with shared nuisance fits; compare target-crossing uncertainty against the retained method.
sources.purpose: Bias correction and pointwise/uniform inference without undersmoothing; not a promise that curve point RMSE, derivative RMSE, or crossing success will improve.
sources.code_status: Formal article data availability links sim-debiased-inference. Its README requires DebiasedDoseResponse and describes exact pointwise/effect/uniform simulation scripts. Visible simulation repository has 5 commits. Original 1000-simulation remote study is not a local pilot budget.
sources.license: No explicit license identified on the visible simulation repository root. Package DESCRIPTION still has the template text use_mit_license(), use_gpl3_license() or friends to pick a license. Do not label as MIT or copy its source as licensed open source; paper-equation independent reproduction remains possible.
sources.cpu_fit: A small fixed number of replications with cached nuisance predictions is feasible in principle, but full uniform-band nuisance refitting and clustered adaptation must be costed separately. No runtime measured this turn.
conditions: Additional causal assumptions needed beyond adjusted association.
Smoothness, nuisance-rate, conditional-density positivity and empirical-process conditions.
The repeated-user implementation needs cluster-aware inference; iid bands cannot simply be advertised as valid for repeated events.

single_candidate_minimal_development_des.question: With exactly the same nuisance predictions and DR pseudo-outcomes, does global curvature-penalized spline final smoothing improve the continuous population compensation-effect curve over the retained Gaussian local-linear final smoothing?
comparison: Retained Kennedy DR local-linear final smoother
Same DR nuisance fits and pseudo-outcomes, cubic smoothing-spline final smoother
freeze: Freeze part 1, covariates, user folds, GPS, nuisance outcome learner, compensation range, reference dose and target before comparison.
No DML, hurdle, direct-derivative or graph-choice search in this experiment.
Use genuinely new development users/seeds and mechanism families; old final batches may explain error but cannot select lambda or methods.
single_candidate_minimal_development_des.development_budget: A small paired development pilot: 3 fresh independent seed blocks times 4 predeclared mechanisms, 180 users and two events per mechanism. Include smooth saturated, nonmonotone, zero-effect, and covariate-dependent assignment with overlapping support. Use cluster folds and a small fixed lambda set after amount/outcome scaling; select once on development. These counts describe a pilot, not a powered accuracy certification.
truth_and_metrics: Primary: effect-curve RMSE in seconds on a predeclared evaluation range, all designed curves included; report valid full-range output separately.
Score population-level curve and dose-specific maxima, not just average integrated fit.

Diagnostic: derivative RMSE with analytic true derivative; crossing reached/not-reached confusion and crossing amount error conditional on a true separated crossing; group curve error plus support/output rate.
Include zero-effect curves, flat near-target curves, and multiple crossings in the later fixed evaluation rather than selecting only easy crossings.
Never count repeated users, paired mechanisms or dense query points as independent seeds.
single_candidate_minimal_development_des.selection: Proceed to one untouched confirmation only if a predeclared practically useful primary gain is observed without reducing output/support or worsening zero-effect target false positives. Lock candidate and lambda policy before confirmation. If point-curve gain occurs with worse derivatives or crossings, report those separately rather than claiming whole-chain improvement.
single_candidate_minimal_development_des.why_identifiable_change: Only final stage changes, so a gain can be attributed to smoothing rather than nuisance fit, additional features or altered graph adjustment. This isolates the next research hypothesis.

excluded_or_deferred: The previous continuous DML and soft two-part candidates already failed held-out adoption; no retuning on those final data.
No claim of a new 2025 Bonvini/Kennedy/Fisher paper: this dose-response paper has two authors and a 2022 first preprint with 2026 revision/publication listing.
No recent conditional dose-response neural learner selected merely for recency. No verified matching primary paper plus licensed implementation was established in this focused search.

Positive-outcome support is not required for continuous conditional means; zero/full-duration atoms do not by themselves invalidate mean-curve methods. Weak treatment support is a separate identification issue.

Do not claim that pooling subgroups on the current population pseudo-outcome automatically estimates subgroup curves: the marginalization and weighting target must be re-derived for conditional groups.
